subject: health
unitTitle: How My Body Works and Stays Well
title: Application or project: dental and skin care
essentialQuestion: How do my body systems and my daily habits work together to keep me well?
materials: paper and pencil or an accessible response tool
the fictional lesson cards included in this task
keyPoints: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between teeth.
Plaque is a bacterial film; left alone it causes decay and gum disease.
Skin needs washing, sun protection, and clean cuts covered to keep germs out.
Adult teeth are permanent, so damage now lasts.
privacySafeScenario: All required evidence uses fictional or public situations. The learner never has to disclose personal health, body, treatment, feelings, family, sexual, or substance-use information.
studentTask: Write two facts. Use the lesson idea about dental and skin care. Choose one safe next step. Name an adult or help source.
knowledgeCheck: Name the fact. Fix the wrong claim. Choose a safe action. Name who can help.
completionCriteria: I explain dental and skin care.
I choose a safe action and give a reason.
I name the right kind of help.
adaptationChoices: Show one short direction at a time. Allow reading aloud, word cards, typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking. Help may repeat a direction but may not choose the fact, action, reason, or help source.
extensionChallenge: Create a new fictional or public case about dental and skin care. Include enough facts, choices or constraints, and support authority for another learner to reason safely. Add an accurate explanation of acceptable variation; use no real person's private information.
accessibilitySupports: Show one action at a time.
Offer a vocabulary card and extra time.
Accept typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking for equal credit.
trustedAdultNote: If a real situation feels unsafe or raises a health concern, pause the lesson and tell a parent, guardian, teacher, school staff member, or another trusted adult. A qualified health professional gives medical advice. In an emergency, get an adult and use the local emergency service.

optionalReflection.prompt: Optional and private: Make up one example that helps you remember dental and skin care. Keep it for yourself. You do not need to show it or prove that you completed it.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, body-fat percentage, body comparison, or appearance scoring.
This task never requires calorie counting, dieting, or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires sharing medical history, a diagnosis, treatment, medication, feelings, family conflict, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires advice about an individual learner's treatment, medication, food, supplement, or exercise plan.
standards: Michigan Health Practice 3: Information and Resource Seeking
Michigan Health Practice 5: Self-Management and Goal Setting
Michigan Health Topic (Grades 3-5): Personal Health and Wellness
learningGoal: I can explain dental and skin care, use facts, choose a safe next step, and name who can help.

lessonExperience.learnerTitle: Learn and apply: dental and skin care
lessonExperience.privacyNotice: Write only about the made-up people. Keep private information private.

entryCheck.heading: Start with a fact
entryCheck.directions: Choose the sentence that states a fact.
choices: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between teeth.
This one detail proves everything about a person's health.
A popular statement about dental and skin care needs no evidence.
entryCheck.support: A fact is stated in the lesson or supported by reliable evidence. An assumption adds a conclusion the information cannot establish.
entryCheck.treatment: This entry check is unscored. Use the support or prerequisite route before continuing when needed.

explanation.heading: Understand dental and skin care
paragraphs: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between teeth.
Plaque is a bacterial film; left alone it causes decay and gum disease.
Skin needs washing, sun protection, and clean cuts covered to keep germs out.
Adult teeth are permanent, so damage now lasts.
explanation.importantDistinction: Learning about dental and skin care supports accurate reasoning and safe next steps; it does not authorize a diagnosis, individualized treatment advice, a person label, or a value judgment.
explanation.decisionRule: DEFINE the public or fictional need. USE accurate evidence. BUILD a feasible response. CHECK authority, access, privacy, and impact.

vocabulary.heading: Words for dental and skin care

terms.meaning: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between teeth.
terms.boundary: This idea does not diagnose, label, or determine the value of a person.

terms.meaning: facts or reliable evidence that can change the interpretation, choice, or next step
terms.boundary: A guess, popularity, or a personal judgment is not relevant evidence by itself.

terms.meaning: the responsible adult, qualified professional, service, or public authority able to help with the situation
terms.boundary: Naming a support route does not make the learner responsible for diagnosis, treatment, or emergency management.

vocabularyCheck.heading: Check the words
vocabularyCheck.selfCheck: A complete check uses the meaning of dental and skin care, one accurate fact, and the responsible support route without labeling a person.

canonicalPracticeContext.heading: Use the authored practice situation
canonicalPracticeContext.situation: A friend brushes once a day and never cleans between their teeth, and their gums bleed. Explain what is likely happening and what to change.
canonicalPracticeContext.treatment: This canonical context may support teaching or discussion. It does not replace the separate fresh independent, mastery, or remediation-retry cases.

modelExample.heading: Watch the reasoning: dental and skin care
modelExample.situation: A fictional Northside youth council is designing a public resource about dental and skin care. It has this approved evidence: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between teeth. The resource must name its audience, a feasible action, the actor with authority, an access or privacy safeguard, and a measure of impact.
relevantFacts: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between teeth.
Plaque is a bacterial film; left alone it causes decay and gum disease.
modelExample.assumptionOrDistraction: A popular or confident statement about dental and skin care is not automatically accurate and cannot establish a person's health, motives, or character.
possibleActions: Build the bounded public resource with evidence, authority, safeguards, and a measure.
Require a real personal health plan.
Publish a claim without checking evidence or access.
modelExample.successCheck: The model uses the lesson fact, explains the connection, stays within the learner role, and names responsible help when it is needed.
workedReasoning: Define one bounded fictional or public need and the audience affected.
Use the lesson fact, identify the actor with authority, and propose a feasible response.
Add an access or privacy safeguard and a measure that could show whether the response worked.

guidedReasoning.heading: Try a different case with support
guidedReasoning.situation: A fictional Riverside youth group must explain or act on dental and skin care. The group has this reliable lesson information: Plaque is a bacterial film; left alone it causes decay and gum disease. It has not been given any person's private health information.
availableChoices: Use the stated facts and compare safe options.
Pause and contact the responsible help source.
turnOne: Name an adult who can help.
guidedReasoning.cue: Look for the situation, safe choices, relevant information, and who can help.
feedbackMoves: If a response adds a guess, replace it with a fact from the case or lesson.
If dental and skin care is named without explanation, link one fact to the concept or process.
If a choice is reasonable but the reason is missing, add the fact that supports it.
If a response seeks disclosure, diagnoses, shames, or exceeds the learner role, switch to the fictional facts and the approved help route.
Accept an equivalent typed, handwritten, drawn-and-labeled, signed, selected, or spoken response when it shows the same reasoning.
guidedReasoning.turnTwo: Fix one sentence. Use a fact and a safe next step.
guidedReasoning.releaseCondition: Continue when the response uses a stated fact, applies dental and skin care, and gives a safe next step without private disclosure or a person label.

independentEvidence.heading: Show what you know on a fresh case
independentEvidence.situation: A fictional Maple Community Center requests a bounded public resource about dental and skin care. Use this evidence: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between teeth. Define the audience and need, propose a feasible action, identify authority, add an access or privacy safeguard, and define a measure.
directions: Use the lesson idea about dental and skin care.
Name an adult or help source.
permittedSupports: read-aloud or one direction at a time
typing, writing, drawing with labels, signing, selecting, or speaking
independentEvidence.independenceBoundary: Support may restate a direction or provide access. It may not choose the controlling fact, conclusion, action, reason, safety judgment, or help route.
successCriteria: I explain dental and skin care.
I choose a safe action and give a reason.
I name the right kind of help.

freshMasteryCheck.heading: Check the idea in a new place
freshMasteryCheck.situation: A fictional Lakeside school committee reviews dental and skin care. The committee knows: Skin needs washing, sun protection, and clean cuts covered to keep germs out. It must correct one unsupported claim and choose a safe next step.
freshMasteryCheck.freshnessNote: This case is different from the model, guided case, and independent case. Do not copy their conclusions.

remediation.heading: Try a different model
remediation.trigger: Use this route after an observable gap in a fact, vocabulary meaning, reasoning step, process order, or help route for dental and skin care.
remediation.prerequisite: First restate this approved fact in your own words: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between teeth.
remediation.alternateExplanation: Use a bridge diagram: NEED and EVIDENCE are one side; ACTION, AUTHORITY, SAFEGUARD, and MEASURE are the spans. A proposal cannot cross the bridge when one span is missing.
contrast: Sufficient: uses a stated fact about dental and skin care, explains the connection, and stays within the learner role.
Needs revision: repeats a topic word, adds a guess, or gives an action with no factual reason or responsible help source.
remediation.guidedCorrection: Cross out the guess. Circle the fact. Add one safe action.

freshRetry.situation: A fictional Oak Street library receives a new question about dental and skin care. Staff provide this approved fact: Plaque is a bacterial film; left alone it causes decay and gum disease. The learner must respond without using the Northside, Riverside, Maple, or Lakeside conclusions.

remediation.exitCriterion: Return to the independent route when the learner accurately uses a fact, applies dental and skin care, explains a safe response, and identifies support without answer-bearing help.
remediation.nextRoute: If the same gap remains, return to the named prerequisite with an adult instructor; do not replace the task with private reflection.

laterTransfer.timing: Use in a later lesson or a separate session.
laterTransfer.prompt: Apply dental and skin care to a meaningfully different fictional or public case. Retrieve the concept, use relevant facts, justify a safe response, and identify the responsible support or authority route.
laterTransfer.masteryBoundary: The current independent response is one evidence occasion. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence now and accurate later retrieval or transfer.

contentProvenance.objective: Apply dental and skin care to the unit performance task and justify the choices made.
